page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 48-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz with one thread per physical core, supported by a 128 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation provides 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations show high multi-threaded compute capability and memory throughput. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 22118.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 99348.93, placing it in upper tiers for parallel workloads. Its memory subsystem delivers 463.49 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 198.92 GB/sec in writes, reflected in a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3334.28. Database handling is particularly strong, scoring 36588.41 on PassMark database operations and executing 89.81 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the architecture lies in single-threaded performance, where the Neoverse-N2 core registers moderate results such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1704.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2075.08. Furthermore, the absence of hardware accelerators limits large-scale machine learning, as shown by a 70B parameter model text generation rate of 4.07 tokens per second. Cost efficiency is driven by the high density of dedicated physical cores paired directly with high-capacity local NVMe storage, making the instance well suited for in-memory caching, relational databases, Clang-based software build clusters, and high-throughput static web serving.

It pairs 192.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core) with 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute capacity, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 22118.0 and high memory bandwidth of 463.49 GB/sec for uncached reads. Database execution is also notable, generating 89.81 million Redis SET operations per second alongside top-tier PassMark database operation scores. While single-thread execution is average, the platform offers favorable resource density for multi-threaded systems. The instance is suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving clusters, and multi-core compilation workloads.
